p1: [low, ominous] In eighteen seventy-two, a ship was found drifting across the Atlantic... [whispers] with nobody on board.
[low] Her name was... the Mary Celeste.
[low] On November seventh, she left New York for Genoa, Italy. Ten people aboard.
[low] A month later, the crew of the Dei Gratia spotted her near the Azores.
[low, tense] They climbed aboard. [whispers] Nobody was there.
[low] The ship was seaworthy. There was still food and water.
[low] The crew's belongings were still in their quarters.
[low] More than seventeen hundred barrels of alcohol... still in the hold.
[low, ominous] But the only lifeboat... was gone.
[low] So were the captain's navigation instruments.
[low] One of the pumps had been taken apart. There were over three feet of water in the hold.
[low] The last log entry... November twenty-fifth. [whispers] After that... nothing.
[low] A court in Gibraltar found no sign of foul play.
[low, ominous] So why would ten people leave a safe ship... [whispers] for one small boat?
[low, ominous] None of them... were ever seen again.
